newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs outperform Germany, dismiss Bfr blues.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs outperform Germany, dismiss Bfr blues.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, who had been lagging other markets on Tuesday, quickly caught up with Bunds on Wednesday as players shrugged off the recent Belgian franc weakening.
At 0815 GMT, the franc was quoted at 20.6390/10 to the mark, well above its 20.6255 ERM midpoint.
"As long as it has absolutely no influence on short-term rates, it will certainly not affect bonds. People are not worried by the 20.64 level," said Dirk Laenen at CERA Bank.
The franc's gentle slide had started mid-April and brought the currency back to the lows seen in February.
The 10-year 2007 OLO was yielding 5.82 percent, against 5.83 on Tuesday, after earlier touching 5.81 percent.
The OLO/Bund yield spread narrowed to 10 basis points from 11 on Tuesday.
"Yesterday we were lagging a bit and now we've just been gradually catching up. It's not really significant," Laenen said.
Traders said activity was moderate and mainly focusing on the five and 10-year area.
"It's mainly switching, people playing the curve a bit," one said. -- Bert Lauwers, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6815, Fax +32 2 230 7710
